holds.excerpt: The ignition control module (ICM) should also be tested, as it can cause similar symptoms.
Always retract the EPB using the maintenance/service mode (scan tool or owner's-manual procedure) before rear pad service.
Diagnose with a scanner for C2005 / C112A-type motor-position codes, then inspect the actuator connector for bent or corroded pins (a frequently overlooked fix) before condemning the motor.
After replacement the battery must be registered/i-stop re-initialized (disconnect-and-relearn or scan tool) so the charging system manages it correctly.
P111A
First replace the fob coin-cell batteries (both keys) and re-test.
If red flashing continues, test another compatible cool device under the same conditions.
If the indicator is solid red, or a verified compatible device still fails after the conditions are met, have Mazda diagnose the charger by VIN.

If the VIN is not covered or the drain remains, fully charge the 12V battery, test its condition and charging strategy, measure key-off current only after all modules have had time to sleep, and isolate the circuit that remains awake.
Replace the 12V battery only if it fails the appropriate test, using the exact installed specification for that powertrain and completing any required battery initialisation.
Repeatedly discharged batteries should be tested because deep discharge can cause permanent capacity loss.
An OBD scanner or oil-and-filter bundle is not the repair for either condition.
If safe and permitted by the manual, retry once after waiting and test a known-good compatible charging point to isolate the supply from the vehicle.
A red indicator, charge warning, repeated failure on multiple known-good stations, or damaged port requires an authorised high-voltage diagnosis.

If usable energy or actual EV distance falls abruptly under comparable conditions, charge disappears while parked, a warning appears, or EV mode repeatedly cancels without a documented reason, ask Mazda for campaign status, high-voltage-battery state-of-health data, charging history, relevant DTCs, and BECM diagnosis.

If P0AA6:00 remains after the campaign software is completed, Mazda's bulletin says the vehicle must be diagnosed for a genuine insulation fault rather than assuming every recurrence is false detection.
Scan all powertrain modules and complete only the Mazda-directed programming, initial learning, or adaptation procedure that applies to that VIN.
Diagnose any remaining instrument blackout, low-12V warning, no-restart, or drivability symptom under its own stored faults and applicable campaign;
If symptoms remain after the recall, return for steering diagnosis rather than assuming a full rack is required.
For wired testing, use the correct USB port and a known-good Apple-approved or phone-manufacturer-approved data cable;
test another compatible phone to separate a phone problem from a vehicle problem.
Have the battery fully charged and tested with Mazda's specified procedure;
Diagnosis and reprogramming are covered under the hybrid/powertrain warranty;
Until repaired, refuel earlier than the gauge suggests.
Mazda Connect can turn SBS off as a temporary risk-control choice while arranging diagnosis, but that removes collision-mitigation assistance and is not a repair.
a red vehicle indicator or a fault that persists after the manual checks requires Mazda diagnosis.
A trained repairer should read charging-system faults and determine whether the problem follows the supply equipment or the vehicle before naming an OBC, inlet, lead-acid battery, or cable.
Diagnosis and reprogramming are covered under warranty;
Reset the coupling adaptation with a Mazda scan tool after service.
P0DAB
Until repaired, refuel earlier than the gauge suggests and track mileage rather than relying on the gauge or range-to-empty estimate.
run the KOEO EVAP test;
locate other leaks with the specified detector or smoke-test process;
and test purge-valve gas tightness.
For P0441, run Mazda's KOER purge-flow self-test.
Replace the purge solenoid only if it fails the stated sealing or flow test, then repeat the EVAP test.
If the freeze-frame pattern does not match, follow normal misfire diagnosis for ignition coils, plugs, injectors, compression, vacuum leaks, fuel quality, and other causes.
If neither bulletin applies, follow Mazda's symptom diagnosis rather than ordering a used or generic CMU from this card.
Test the battery and replace if it has been deeply discharged.
diagnosis, current coverage and the VIN-specific service part must be confirmed.
Perform a boost leak test with a pressurized adapter at every 30,000-mile interval.
Diagnose by sliding cardboard under the engine and noting where drips land — rear means CAS O-ring, front means front crank seal, sides/top means valve cover.
Diagnose by measuring crankshaft endplay with a dial indicator at the front pulley while an assistant works the clutch pedal: more than ~0.008 in.
Diagnose specific component — motor, cable, or latch.
Diagnose with a Mazda scan tool to identify the specific failed component (sensor, module, or motor).
Test output voltage at the battery (should be 13.8-14.4V) and load test the battery, which may have been damaged by the failing alternator.

Clean and refresh every factory ground point (shock tower, starter/bell-housing, ECU grounds), protect them with dielectric grease, and add supplemental 8-10 gauge ground straps from the engine and chassis to the battery negative — forum consensus is this cures the hesitation about 90% of the time.
Until fixed, keep the exhaust restriction stock and watch a known-accurate boost gauge.
Diagnose with a rotary compression test (a rotary-specific tester reading all three faces per rotor;
Replace a clogged cat with a fresh high-flow catalytic converter (or a test/replacement pipe where legal) and correct any upstream oil or fuel cause so the new unit isn't destroyed.
Have injectors flow-tested and cleaned if budget is tight, but old injector tips typically need replacement on a 20+ year old FD.
Pressure-test the vacuum system to locate leaks.
Bench-test each solenoid for proper actuation;
Diagnose with misfire codes P0300-P0304 before replacing.

Replace with a higher-capacity battery (many owners fit a ~640 CCA unit of the same case dimensions), use a battery tender when parked, and diagnose/repair any abnormal parasitic draw or a failing alternator.
Some owners use high-flow aftermarket cats or test pipes for track use.
